issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Milkable interface (with messageOnMilk()), however the solution introduces an interface named Dairy (with messageOnMilk()) and leaves Milkable.java empty. Classes in the solution (Seal, Goat) implement Dairy instead of Milkable, while the template Main and the UML/spec expect Milkable. This naming/type mismatch can confuse students and cause compilation or integration issues when following the exercise (e.g., code expecting Milkable won't match the solution's Dairy).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (or remove the empty Milkable.java and implement it as Milkable), and update all classes (Seal, Goat) to implement Milkable. Ensure Milkable.java contains the messageOnMilk() method signature so it matches the UML and the template Main usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (and student code examples use Milkable), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' and leaves a separate Milkable.java file empty. This is the same conceptual entity (animals that can be milked) being referenced with two different identifiers across artifacts, which will confuse students mapping the requirement 'Milkable' to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (or replace the empty Milkable.java with the content of Dairy.java) and update all classes to implement 'Milkable'. Ensure the solution does not include both 'Dairy' and an empty 'Milkable' to avoid ambiguity.
